When the baseline metric is negative, for example an R² below 0, dividing by the signed value reverses the comparison: with a baseline R² of -1.8 and a 5% gate, a worse candidate at -5.0 passes and a perfect candidate at 1.0 fails. This PR divides by `abs(baseline)` for both greater-is-better and lower-is-better metrics. Results for positive baselines are unchanged, and the zero-baseline path is untouched (`_validate` already falls back to a plain comparison there). The `MetricThreshold` docstring gave the rule as `baseline * (1 + min_relative_change)`, which is also wrong for negative baselines. It now reads `baseline + min_relative_change * abs(baseline)` (and the lower-is-better counterpart), with a note that this equals the old formula when the baseline is positive. ### How is this PR tested? - [x] Existing unit/integration tests - [x] New unit/integration tests `test_validation_relative_threshold_uses_baseline_magnitude` in `tests/evaluate/test_validation.py` adds 26 cases: the R² example above, plus candidates 50%, 20% and 5% better and worse than baselines of -2.0 and 2.0, for both metric directions. Implement the following change in this repository. Do not install dependencies or run the full test suite; run the tests relevant to your change if you want to. Make the code change (and adjust or add a test if it is natural), then summarize what you changed and why. ### Related Issues/PRs Relates to #25550 ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? A custom scorer defined with the `@scorer` decorator carries its function source in its serialized form. Reconstructing such a scorer runs that source through `exec()`, so deserializing one executes user-provided code. Until now this happened wherever a scorer was deserialized, including inside the tracking server process (the scorer-invoke handler, online-scoring config validation, and gateway guardrail loading). This change confines that code execution to the job executor: - In the tracking server process, a custom scorer is deserialized as **non-executing metadata**. It carries the scorer's fields and its serialized form (so the server can inspect it and forward it to the executor) but running it raises. The server never executes custom scorer code. - In the job executor subprocess, the scorer is reconstructed and run as before. Reconstruction is enabled only around the executor entrypoints. - A client process (for example, a user loading a registered scorer to run it locally) reconstructs scorers exactly as before. The three process contexts are distinguished as follows. The server sets a per-boot marker in the worker environment, and its subprocesses inherit it, so a process can tell whether it belongs to the server. A separate internal marker is set only around reconstruction in the executor entrypoints. Reconstruction is allowed when that executor marker is present or when the process is not a server process; otherwise it is refused. This refusal is enforced at the single reconstruction function as well, so the server cannot execute custom scorer code even if a new call site is added later. For defense in depth, the server forces the executor marker off for its workers so it can never be inherited from the ambient environment. Gateway guardrails run their scorer directly in the server process. Because the server no longer executes custom scorer code, a custom `@scorer` scorer is rejected as a guardrail: both when a guardrail is created and when one is loaded. Guardrails continue to support built-in scorers and judges created with `make_judge`, which do not execute stored source. The rejection also looks inside scorer ensembles, so an ensemble that embeds a custom scorer is rejected too. A guardrail that already uses a custom scorer (for example, one created on a server that had opted in with `MLFLOW_SERVER_ENABLE_CUSTOM_SCORERS`) now fails requests to its endpoint with a server error naming the guardrail, instead of being silently skipped, so the endpoint never serves traffic without a guardrail it is configured to run. Other guardrail load failures are still skipped and logged as before. ### How is this PR tested? - [x] Existing unit/integration tests - [x] New unit/integration tests - [ ] Manual tests New tests cover: the server returning a non-executing scorer that raises when called and still re-serializes; the executor and client reconstructing normally; the reconstruction function refusing to run in the server process; the executor marker being set and restored around reconstruction; the server forcing that marker off for its workers; detection of custom code including inside ensembles; rejection of custom scorers as guardrails at both creation and load; a gateway request failing with a server error when its endpoint has a custom-scorer guardrail; and the online scoring scheduler skipping disabled custom scorers and routing session-level ones correctly. ### Does this PR require documentation update? - [x] No. - [ ] Yes. I've updated: - [ ] Examples - [ ] API references - [ ] Instructions ### Does this PR require updating the [MLflow Skills](https://github.com/mlflow/skills) repository? - [x] No. - [ ] Yes. Please link the corresponding PR or explain how you plan to update it. ### Release Notes #### Is this a user-facing change? - [ ] No. - [x] Yes. Give a description of this change to be included in the release notes for MLflow users. Custom scorers defined with the `@scorer` decorator are no longer executed in the MLflow tracking server process; their code runs only in the job executor. As a result, a custom `@scorer` scorer can no longer be used as a gateway guardrail (guardrails support built-in scorers and judges). If an endpoint already has a guardrail backed by a custom scorer, requests to that endpoint now fail until the guardrail is removed or replaced with a built-in scorer or a judge. #### What component(s), interfaces, languages, and integrations does this PR affect?
